llm.summary: This is a documentation-only Vitest testing skill with no executable code, hidden behavior, persistence, or data access.

dimensions.detail: The guidance is proportionate to a testing helper skill and does not request credentials, broad filesystem access, network access, account authority, or sensitive local data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains Markdown files only; no install scripts, executable files, dependencies, remote retrieval, or bundled code execution surface were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest lists generic trigger terms such as describe, it, expect, beforeEach, and afterEach, which could cause over-broad activation, but the loaded content is limited to benign testing guidance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanisms, background workers, profile/session access, memory writes, tool wrapping, privilege escalation, or automatic mutation instructions were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently provide Vitest test examples, assertions, mocking, configuration, timers, snapshots, and anti-pattern guidance.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Installers should expect this skill to provide Vitest testing reference material. The only practical caveat is that its broad trigger words may make it appear during ordinary JavaScript testing discussions, but the content itself is documentation-only.
llm.findings:
[MP3] expected: The MOCKING.md finding refers to Vitest mock cleanup methods such as vi.clearAllMocks, vi.resetAllMocks, and vi.restoreAllMocks; this is test mock state cleanup, not agent memory manipulation.
[MP3] expected: The references/mocking.md finding is the same Vitest mock cleanup example and is purpose-aligned testing documentation.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger terms are broad and may invoke the skill in more coding contexts than intended, but they are recognizable Vitest API names and do not introduce sensitive authority or unsafe behavior.
